candidate.claim: The Mellin representation factors the approximation into a zeta quotient and a Mobius Dirichlet sum, so RH is needed only for convergence to reciprocal zeta in the right half-plane; functional symmetry alone controls the later epsilon limit.
candidate.proposed_limit: This separation depends on the L2 isometry and the specific Beurling kernel; it is not automatically an Lp argument.

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The span supplies two analytically different inputs: zero-freeness, with a positive interior margin, controls a partial Möbius Dirichlet sum, while the functional equation and gamma asymptotics control a reflected zeta quotient without RH or Lindelöf. The first is a conditional approximation theorem, not a symmetry; the second is an unconditional growth estimate.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Separates hypothesis accounting and identifies the positive margin δ as the price of uniformity.

accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: No speculation; any later use of the quotient for damping is outside this span and is not asserted here.

parents.title: The Mellin-Plancherel isometry turns closure convergence into a dominated zeta-quotient limit

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Mellin–Plancherel replaces an opaque H-norm convergence question by an L2 domination problem on a spectral line while preserving exactly the norm at issue. The transform factors the approximant into zeta, a partial reciprocal-zeta approximation, and a linear denominator; RH-dependent estimates provide domination, while a separate x>1 bound is still needed to remove the auxiliary weight.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Tracks what the representation preserves, what arithmetic factors it exposes, and why convergence after multiplication by x^{-ε} is insufficient by itself.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted; the mechanism and RH-dependent proof burden are explicit, with exact transform normalization reserved for formula verification.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span defines an invertible Fourier–Mellin isometry H→K, computes the transformed damped approximants, invokes Littlewood and Lemmas 2.1–2.2 plus the RH-implied Lindelöf bound, applies dominated convergence for ε<1/4, and then uses (2.9) to recover convergence of the unweighted functions.

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: At this local limit-removal stage, the reflected zeta quotient supplies an unconditional spectral majorant as ε tends to zero. The Mellin isometry transfers convergence back to H, a similar tail argument removes the weight, and the already established pointwise identity fixes the norm limit as −χ. Locally unconditional does not mean the upstream theorem is unconditional.
